remaining.title: Embedding a subsetted Unicode font (fontkit) so CJK, Hebrew, Arabic and emoji print properly
remaining.why: It cannot be done properly under the no-new-dependency rule. pdf-lib needs fontkit to embed anything but the 14 standard faces, the font the app already ships is .woff2 (fontkit cannot read woff2 without a Brotli decoder), and a CJK-capable face is several megabytes of vendored binary in an offline-first app. I took the fix list's stated minimum instead — transliterate everything transliterable and report the rest loudly, in the app before export and on the PDF itself — and left the CSV/.json as the lossless path. Polish, Czech, Turkish, Baltic, Cyrillic and Greek now print correctly; CJK/Hebrew/Arabic/emoji still render '?' but are counted and named.

remaining.title: Several photos per item
remaining.why: Named as an aside inside the close-up fix. It is a model, capture-UI, dialog, PDF-layout and ZIP-naming change all at once, and doing it badly would have put half a feature into the record shape that the CSV columns are now built on. The close-up pipeline plus the receipt/close-up slot (two full-resolution images per item) shipped; a real gallery is the next round's work.

remaining.title: A full 'After a loss' mode
remaining.why: It is in mostWantedNext rather than the ordered fix list, and a proper version is a second product mode (recall prompts, camera hidden, no photo-completeness grading, CSV-first export). I did the cheap parts of Marcus's complaint instead: the app reopens on whichever tab you left it on rather than presenting a camera every time, the tab no longer carries a 📷, the PDF placeholder reads 'photo not taken' rather than grading the row, and the CSV/quantity/condition/replacement-cost fields he actually needs now exist.

remaining.title: Moving photos into a separate IndexedDB object store
remaining.why: The measured problem — 514ms of blocked main thread per keystroke — is entirely fixed by taking the snapshot inside the debounce (now 0–1ms for 10 keystrokes with 200 photographed items). Splitting the store is a data-migration change to every existing user's record and would have to be reversible; it is not worth that risk for a cost that is now unmeasurable.

remaining.title: Making the room-filter chips sticky as well as the tab strip
remaining.why: Only nav.tabs is sticky. Two stacked sticky strips at 320px with Largest text would eat roughly 200px of a 568px screen, which costs Dee more than it gains her. The tab strip — the one that was scrolling away and the one that reaches Export — is pinned.
